bull.t: Revenue rebound and high gross margin
bull.b: The strong revenue rebound and very high gross margin indicate that ProQR can generate substantial value from collaborations and licensing when programs advance. If this growth continues, it could provide increasing resources for research while preserving attractive economics on successful partnered programs.

A sizable cash balance and runway into mid-2028 give ProQR time to advance several clinical programs without an immediate funding event. This supports sustained investment in the Axiomer platform, allows clinical milestones to mature, and improves negotiating flexibility with potential partners.

The progression of an AI-discovered candidate into human testing, alongside reported efficiency gains, strengthens evidence that Axiomer can generate differentiated programs. A repeatable discovery engine and multiple planned readouts could broaden the pipeline and improve long-term development productivity.

bear.b: Large net losses and deeply negative operating and free cash flow show that ProQR is not yet self-funding. Continued burn can reduce financial flexibility over time, increase dependence on additional capital, and make the company more vulnerable if clinical development takes longer or produces weaker results.

bear.t: Dependence on external capital and collaborations
bear.b: A business model centered on upfront, milestone, and licensing payments creates uneven revenue visibility because cash receipts depend on partner agreements and program progress. Without recurring product sales, ProQR may need further financing or partnerships to sustain development and corporate operations.

Because ProQR has no marketed products, its future revenue and profitability depend on advancing investigational medicines through clinical, regulatory, and commercial stages. This leaves the company without an established product base and makes long-term business performance dependent on development execution.
